2. The substance of averments made in both the Petitions are as under:
That on 03.01.2020 at about 10.30 a.m. the Petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider in a Honda Activa bearing No.KA- V.Gunashekaran vs Naresh C Chawla on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95729861/
2 04-JK-4022 from Vyalikaval to High Court, Bangalore via Seshadripuram Law College.
At that time, a Honda City car bearing No.KA-02-ME-5958 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the Petitioner from left side.
Due to the said impact, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, Petitioner was shifted to Jayashree Nursing Home for first aid treatment and thereafter was referred to Mallige Medical Centre wherein he was treated as an inpatient.

Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as a Law practitioner and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
3.

The Petitioner has contended that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-ME-5958 which is owned by the Respondent No.1, 3 and 4 and insured with Respondent No.2.
As such, the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
4. In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective counsel and filed detailed Objection Statement.
Subsequently Respondent No.3 and 4 were impleaded as the offending vehicle was registered in the name of partnership firm which belongs to Respondent No.1, 3 and 4.
Despite of service of notice the respondents No.3 and 4 remained absent and was placed exparte.
5. Respondent No.1 has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner.
Further denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver.
He has further denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioner.
He further contended that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-04-JK-4022 by its rider.
The car is insured with the respondent No.
On these grounds, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. Respondent No.2 has denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner.
It has admitted the issuance of policy to car bearing No.KA-02-ME-5958.
Further it contended that owner of the insured car has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
The driver of car had no valid driving licence to drive the car and entrusted the vehicle to a person who had no valid driving licence.
Hence, there was breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further it denied that the accident was caused by the rash and negligent driving of the offending car by its driver.
It has further denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment of the Petitioner.
It further contended that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of Honda Activa bearing No.KA-04-JK-4022 by its rider.
The owner and insurer of the said Honda Activa are proper and necessary parties and the petition is bad for non-joinder of the necessary parties.
On these grounds, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. On the rival pleadings, my Learned Predecessor in office has framed following Issues.

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 03.01.2020 at about 10.30 a.m., at Fresh Nest Shop, near Subramanya Swamy Temple, Seshadripuram, due to the rash and negligent driving of Honda City car bearing No.KA-02-ME-5958?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award ?
8. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 19 documents at Ex.P1 to 18 and 23.
He further got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.P.19 to 22.
On the other hand, the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any evidence.
9. The learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on the following decisions.

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents.
I have perused the depositions, documents exhibited, the decisions relied by the learned counsels and materials available on record.

12. My answer to the Issues are as under :
Issue No. 1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 :
It is the case of the Petitioner that he has sustained injuries in the accident caused by the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-02-ME-5958.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and V.Gunashekaran vs Naresh C Chawla on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95729861/
4 negligent driving of the driver of the offending car.
14.
In order to prove the case, petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked in total 23 documents.

Ex. P-1 to Ex.P-10 are the Certified copies of FIR along with Complaint, Spot panchanama,
charge sheet, spot sketch, statements, notice u/s 133 of MV Act, reply to the said notice and wound certificate.

Ex.P.11 is the certified copy of Order sheet in CC.1637/2020, Ex.P.12 is the prescriptions, Ex.P.13 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.14 is the medical reports, Ex.P.15 is the medical bills, Ex.P.16 is the X-rays with report, Ex.P.17 is attendant charges and Ex.P.18 is notarized copy of Aadhar card.

15. Upon going through the said documents, it shows that on the complaint lodged by one J.Arvind Babu., High Grounds Traffic police have filed FIR against the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-02-ME-5958 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 of IPC.
The document Ex.P2 is the Spot panchanama and Ex.P.4 is the spot sketch
shows that the concerned police have drawn the same in the presence of panchas.

Ex.P.3 is the charge sheet discloses the fact that after thorough investigation, the IO has charge sheeted the driver of offending car in question for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.10 is the Wound Certificate shows that petitioner sustained injuries.

16. Further, P.W.1 examined a witness who was riding the motor bike as PW.2 and also examined Dr.C.Ramesh as P.W.3 and got marked Ex.P.19 to 22 i.e., authorisation letter, disability certificate,
inpatient record and recent X-ray.
The PW.2 deposed about the accident and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

PW.3 who is the medical legal consultant of the hospital re-iterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
17.
To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross- examination P.W.1 has denied the suggestions of the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contentions of the Petitioner.

18. Though the Respondent No.1 and 2 had taken contention that the accident does not caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, it did not lead any evidence to substantiate its contentions.
Moreover, after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending car.
Further more the driver of the offending vehicle has pleaded guilty for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC as per the EX.P11.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 1 in the 'Affirmative'.

19. Issue No. 2 - As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending car by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

5 20.
In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 57 years.
The Petitioner has produced Aadhar card at Ex. P.18 to prove his age.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 13.06.1963.
The accident took place on 03.01.2020.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is 57 years which is to be taken for the purpose of assessment.
21. Further, the Petitioner has averred that he was practicing as Law Practitioner and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to substantiate the said fact.

In the judgments relied by the Learned counsel for petition Union of India & others Vs. Abdul Rashid Nengroo (supra), Hon'ble High Court of Jammu and Kashmir held that :
"12.

sentences.text: The facts of the reported judgment are distinguishable.

In the reported case, the deceased was stated stated to be a businessman dealing in fruits and his income was taken on the basis of statement of a witness, namely,, Nair Ahmad who, in fact, is the deceased but inadvertendly instated of Nazir Ahmad Khan, Nazzir Ahmad Bhat has been referred to.
On facts, case of the claimant is altogether different.

Claimant himself is an advocate, he has appeared as a witness and has in categorical terms testified that he was earning more than Rs.30000 per month, however, he was not an income tax payee as he had to incur lot of expenses on chamber,, etc.
Appellants have led evidence before the Tribunal but there is not even a whisper in the statements of witnesses as against the income of the claimant.
Statement of the claimant as a witness as a whole has remained to be controverted rather repelled, therefore, there was no option open to the Tribunal but to accept the same.

Even otherwise, default in paying income tax would not mean that the income of the claimant is incorrect when the income as claimed is otherwise proved."
Underlined by me 22.
As per the above said authority mere non payment of income tax does not mean that the income of the claimant is incorrect when income as claimed is otherwise proved.
But in the case on hand the petitioner has not proved his income by producing cogent and convincible evidence.
Therefore, the above said authority would not helps the case of petitioner.
Therefore, in the absence of any documentary evidence, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has occurred in the year 2020, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.14,500/- p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
23. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
24.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-10 and other medical records reveal that in the accident the petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1.Left tibia fracture.

6 2.
Left fibula fracture 3.Lacerated wound over medial malleolus 1 x 1 cms.
The Doctor has opined that injury No.1 and 2 are grievous in nature and injury No.3 is simple in nature.
Further, P.W.3 has also re-iterated about the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident.

25. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
II
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
26. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
27.
The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 03.01.2020 and discharged on 07-01-2020 at Mallige Medical Centre.

28. Upon going through the discharge summary at Ex.P- 13 which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 03.01.2020 and discharged on 07-01-2020 at Mallige Medical Centre i.e., for 5 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 5 days.
29. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, atleast it took two months for recovery.
I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as one month.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,000/- under this head (@ Rs.14,500/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
30.
Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period.
The Ex.P.17 receipts 2 in Nos. shows that the Petitioner has engaged an attendant, wherein he paid an amount of Rs.17,000/- towards attendant charge to the BSV Home Care Services.
Further he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.17,000/- towards attendants charges,
Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
31. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent Rs.3,01,000/- towards medical expenses.
He has produced 52 medical bills at Ex.P.15 amounting to Rs.1,10,991/-.

I have gone through the medical V.Gunashekaran vs Naresh C Chawla on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95729861/
7 bills.

sentences.text: The acceptable medical bills totally amounting to Rs.1,10,991/, which is rounded up at Rs.1,10,991/
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,11,000/ as a compensation under this head.

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
32.
The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is unable to carry out his day to day activities.
33. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.C.Ramesh as P.W.3 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked authorisation letter, disability certificate, inpatient record and recent X-ray at Ex.P.19 to 22.
In the cross-examination, PW.3 has stated that he has not treated the petitioner and he is a Medical Legal consultant and not an Orthopedic surgeon.

34. In the judgments relied by the Learned counsel for petition Karunakara Vs. Abdul Rasheed and others (supra) Hon'ble High court of Kerala held that :
Quantum - Injury - Principles of assessment - Disability certificate - Tribunal disregarded the disability certificate issued by the Medical Board on the grounds that certificate was not issued by the doctor who treated the injured and doctor who issued the certificate was not examined-

entities.text: Karunakara Vs. Abdul Rasheed and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Held: there is no binding principle that in order to rely on a disability certificate it should have necessarily been issued by the doctor who treated the injured and there is no hard and fast rule that in all cases the doctor should be examined in order to accept the permanent disability certified by him in respect of a person sustaining injuries in a motor accident; if the Tribunal is satisfied with the reasons stated by the doctor and the permanent disability certified by him then there is no need to examine the doctor.
35. As such there is no bar to rely upon the disability assessment report prepared by non treated doctor.
The petitioner averred that he is practicing as an advocate by profession, due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident he is unable to do work.
But, during his cross examination he specifically admitted that he is continuing his practice as an advocate.
In the judgement relied by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 Subash (supra).

Hon'ble High court of Karnataka held that "Re point 1: as rightly pointed out by learned counsel appearing for insurer, the Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding compensation towards loss of future income, resulting, in serious miscarriage of justice, when in fact, the claimant has been continued in the services of the corporation as 'Conductor'.
If the claimant is continued in service, then, question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.

Therefore taking this aspect into consideration,
without going into further merits and demerits of the case, we hereby set aside the compensation of Rs.1,86,525 awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of future income".
36. In the case on hand as discussed above the petition is continuing the practice as an advocate even after accident.

Hence, it is clear that injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident does V.Gunashekaran vs Naresh C Chawla on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95729861/
8 not come in the way of profession.
Accordingly, the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise at all.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for loss of future earning.
VII COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
37. Petitioner stated in his evidence that, he has to incur towards future medical expenses also.
PW.3 doctor in his evidence has stated that petitioner requires surgery for removal of LC plate and screws and tubular plate inserted, it would cost Rs.1,20,000/- towards surgery.
However, PW-3 has not produced any estimation.

Hence, by considering the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken for the said injuries this Tribunal opined that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of future medical expenses.
Hence, petitioner is entitled of Rs.50,000/- towards Future medical Expenses and this amount does not carry any future interest.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
38.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 50,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 29,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.2,21,000/-
5. Loss of income during the laid Rs. 29,000/-
up period 6
Future treatment Rs. 50,000/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,19,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
39. Regarding Liability
: As already discussed above, in this case the driver of the offending car bearing No.KA-02-ME- 5958 was charge-sheeted.
Further, there is no dispute about the validity of the Insurance Policy of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, Respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No. 2 as "Partly in the Affirmative".
40. Issue No.3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

9 ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No. 1 and 2 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.4,19,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
(The award passed under head of future medical expenses does not carry any interest)
The Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
